extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, reviewers, editors, and educated readers of literary journals
extracted.subtask_description: Norms and evaluative criteria for reviewing literature, editing, translating, and running literary journals — focused on fairness, method, tone, and fidelity to literary merits rather than party or personality. Drawn from a critical essay contrasting editorial practices of contemporary reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue_do_not_denounce
rubrics_metrics.description: He does not refute, but denounces him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should refute opponents' arguments rather than resort to denunciation, caricature, or wholesale stigmatization; avoid wholesale condemnation in place of reasoned rebuttal (example: Mr. Gifford 'does not refute, but denounces').

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality_and_balanced_argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes up a question, and argues it pro and con with great knowledge... states the arguments and circumstances on both sides, from which a judgment is to be formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good review presents and weighs evidence on both sides, states objections honestly, and avoids suppressing counterarguments (contrast Edinburgh Review's practice with that of the Quarterly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge_literary_merits_not_political_credos
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Quarterly nothing is regarded but the political creed or external circumstances of a writer; in the Edinburgh nothing is ever adverted to but his literary merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should assess works on literary/taste grounds rather than on authors' political beliefs or external affiliations; avoid letting party-creed determine literary awards or punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_personal_abuse_and_calumny
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no abuse or corruption that does not there find a Jesuitical palliation or a barefaced vindication... no character that is not slandered, if it can answer the purposes of a party to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from personal attacks, slander, or calumny as substitutes for critique; personal invective is incompatible with trustworthy reviewing (examples: vicious attacks on individual authors described in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual_accuracy_and_honest_quotation
rubrics_metrics.description: He has neither the effrontery nor the meanness to falsify facts or to suppress objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism must be factually reliable: quotations should not be garbled, facts should not be misrepresented, and objections should not be suppressed to manufacture a verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire_should_be_witty_spirited_and_proportionate
rubrics_metrics.description: His satire is mere peevishness and spleen... he expresses a great deal of anger and contempt, but you cannot tell very well why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical criticism ought to show wit, spirit, and proportionate cause; avoid violent, abrupt invective that appears driven by personal rancour rather than by artistic grounds (example: Gifford's violent satire).

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness_to_unconventional_forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial of their beauties, because they were included in no school, because they were reducible to no previous standard or theory of poetical excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss works' merits simply because they do not fit established schools or preconceived standards (example: initial treatment of the Lyrical Ballads); assess novelty on its intrinsic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give_fair_hearing_to_paradoxical_opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: He is bound to lend a patient hearing to the most paradoxical opinions and extravagant theories which have resulted in our times from the 'infinite agitation of wit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/reviewers should patiently consider bold or paradoxical ideas, subjecting them to reasoned checks and practical objections rather than outright dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connected_reasoning_and_original_illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: He has shown no striking power of analysis nor of original illustration... his observations are petty, ill-concocted, and discover as little tact, as they do a habit of connected reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical writing should display coherent analysis and original insight that illuminate an author's character and spirit; avoid disconnected, petty, or ill-formed observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing_scholarly_texts_with_care_but_without_partisan_notes
rubrics_metrics.description: As an editor of old authors, Mr. Gifford is entitled to considerable praise for the pains he has taken in revising the text, and for some improvements... he had better have spared the notes, in which... he has exposed his own ill-temper and narrowness of feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly editing should focus on accurate revision and useful improvements to the text; editorial notes should not become vehicles for partisan spite or personal narrowness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation_quality_fidelity_not_bald_offensive_rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Gifford's version of the Roman satirist is the baldest, and, in parts, the most offensive of all others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations should aim for fidelity, literary skill, and good taste; avoid flat, inelegant, or offensively rendered versions that betray the translator's lack of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role_of_journals_promote_free_inquiry_not_partisan_propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Its object is to poison the sources of public opinion and of individual fame — to pervert literature... into an engine of priestcraft and despotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals should be instruments of free discussion, liberty, and humanity rather than organs of political sophistry, patronage, or personal calumny; editors must not use journals to pervert public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_infering_doctrinal_belief_from_poetic_imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: He insists on the profusion of crucifixes, glories, angelic visions... as evidence of the theological sentiments meant to be inculcated by the play, when the least reflection might have taught him, that they proved nothing but the author's poetical conception of the character and costume of his subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat poetic ornamentation or imagery as definitive proof of an author's theological or political creed; distinguish poetic conception from doctrinal advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone_manly_explicitness_and_candour
rubrics_metrics.description: They are eminently characteristic of the Spirit of the Age; as it is the express object of the Quarterly Review to discountenance and extinguish that spirit... We must do justice to the talent with which they are supported, and to the tone of manly explicitness in which they are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism benefits from a frank, explicit, and candid tone that addresses questions on their merits; this tone contrasts with trimming or evasive partiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_patronage_driven_authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The weight of power, of wealth, of rank is thrown into the scale... and the whole is under the guidance of Mr. Gifford's instinctive genius — of the in-born hatred of servility for independence...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and journals should not rely on patronage, rank, or power to manufacture authority or to blacklist competitors; literary reputation should not be produced by black-balling or partisan favour.
